sites.name: OpenVibe.Chat
sites.tagline: One chat for the whole network.
sites.description: OpenVibe.Chat is the chat service of the OpenVibe network. It already runs the chat on OpenVibe.Live: global and stream chat, direct messages and text-to-speech. openvibe.chat is planned as its own home: rooms that span every OpenVibe site, group rooms and voice, one identity for every conversation.
pillars: Rooms that span every OpenVibe site, with the same moderation tools everywhere.
DMs and group rooms tied to your OpenVibe account, not to one website.
Voice rooms and streamer-to-viewer calls, the same engine Live uses today.
Text-to-speech, soundboards and audio queues for streams and rooms.
meanwhile: The global chat is already live there — same account, same rules.
Voice rooms run inside Live's chat today.
sites.keywords: openvibe chat, community chat, voice rooms, direct messages, free speech chat
sites.launch: its own web client at this address; the service already runs the chat on OpenVibe.Live

Read the same story from several perspectives, side by side.
You choose the lens; nothing is chosen for you silently.
Follow topics across sources, with your OpenVibe account.

sites.name: OpenVibe.Host
sites.description: OpenVibe.Host is the network's deployment tooling and, next, static site hosting for OpenVibe projects. The tooling (ovhost) already runs on the network's host: deploys with automatic rollback, backups and restore drills for the network's own services. The hosting part will let a project upload a folder of HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images, serve it at <site>.openvibe.host and roll back to any earlier deploy in one step. Static files only: nothing uploaded is run as code.
pillars: Upload a folder or a .tar.gz of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images and fonts; it is served at <site>.openvibe.host over HTTPS.
Deploys are immutable and content-addressed: switch to, or roll back to, any earlier one in one step.
Custom domains you prove with a DNS TXT record; their certificates are issued by an operator for now.
No build step and no server-side code: nothing you upload is run. Running bots, mods or apps is not offered; that needs isolation the network has not built yet.
meanwhile: The code, the launch checklist and the threat review.
Projects, apps and credentials on OpenVibe.Codes, the developer portal.
sites.keywords: openvibe host, static site hosting, deployment, openvibe projects
sites.launch: the owner's go on its launch checklist

sites.name: OpenRe.Stream
sites.tagline: Ingest and restream, in the open.
sites.description: OpenRe.Stream is the ingest and restream service split out of OpenVibe.Live: RTMP ingest with stream keys and lifecycle, and restreaming to RTMP, RTMPS and SRT destinations, with WHIP to follow. Broadcasters still go live through OpenVibe.Live until their stream moves over.
pillars: RTMP ingest with keys and lifecycle in one place; WHIP/WebRTC and SRT ingest to follow.
Twitch, YouTube, Kick and any RTMP, RTMPS or SRT destination.
Live acknowledgement, errors relayed in plain words, uptime.
Run it yourself; the code is on GitHub.
meanwhile: Ingest and restreaming run inside Live today.
sites.keywords: openre stream, rtmp ingest, whip, srt, restream, open source streaming infrastructure

Discovery, JWKS and standard ID tokens for any relying party.

meanwhile: The live sign-in flow, used by every OpenVibe site today.
The OpenID configuration Network publishes today.

sites.name: realtime.openvibe.network
sites.tagline: Closed: realtime delivery is part of OpenVibe.Events.
sites.description: OpenVibe.Realtime was planned as a separate service for live updates in the browser. Decision record ADR-005 (accepted 2026-09-22) closed it: browser realtime is part of OpenVibe.Events, as server-sent events with cursor resume at events.openvibe.network/realtime/stream. This address serves only this notice.
sites.linksLead: Realtime delivery for browsers is a part of OpenVibe.Events; the decision and its record are public.
links: Durable events, subscriptions and signed delivery; browsers subscribe at /realtime/stream.
The decision, and when a separate realtime service would be reconsidered.
The repository stays as the decision record.
sites.keywords: openvibe realtime, openvibe events, server-sent events
